They also asked for:

- SIG-lite answers to high-risk controls,
- Confirmation of the expected delivery date for a SOC 2 Type II report if not already available.

Can Redwood provide a signed bridge letter on corporate letterhead and state an expected Type II delivery date? Procurement has specifically asked whether a CEO-signed + notarized bridge is acceptable (they said they "prefer notarized").

We are trying to close this by the 2nd week of Sep to get the contract processed before their mid-quarter close. If you need a single point of contact on our side: I am the procurement lead (Rajiv).

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping — I understand the urgency. Proposed fast path (48–72h initial turnaround for documents):

1) Bridge letter (signed by CEO) — security will draft language confirming the scope of controls in place, plus an auditor statement of engagement schedule. Legal will review for notarization requirements. Target: draft by Sep 9, CEO sign + e-notary by Sep 13 if legal signs off on e-notarization.

2) CAIQ snapshot — we can export a current CAIQ for Q2 2027 and redact any irrelevant internal notes. Attached: CAIQ-snapshot-2027Q2.json.

3) SIG-lite / high-risk controls matrix — we will produce concise answers for procurement (2-pager).

4) Evidence package — Rishi, please pull the audit-evidence-checklist I attached and assign owners. We'll provide a zipped evidence bundle on a secure share. Attached: audit-evidence-checklist.xlsx.

Notes on notarization: full physical notarization adds lead time and may require courier. Many customers accept e-notarization + DocuSign certificate; we should confirm FinStart's tolerance.

If procurement insists on a "notarized" wet signature only, Legal will need to coordinate with an external notary service — expect added 3–5 business days.

I'll start the bridge draft now and ping Legal for the notarization bit.

-Vivek
